gloss: To see the whole cow; to focus so intently that other details are ignored.
teaser: Have you ever been so focused on one thing that you missed everything else?
script: Welcome to Chengyu Bites — your quick summary on Chinese 成语. Have you ever been so focused on one thing that you missed everything else? [break 1s] The phrase is: 目无全牛, mù wú quán niú. [break 0.5s] 目 (mù) - eye [break 0.5s] 无 (wú) - without [break 0.5s] 全 (quán) - whole [break 0.5s] 牛 (niú) - cow [break 0.5s] The full idiom again: 目无全牛, which literally means 'to see the whole cow' and figuratively refers to being so focused on one detail that one overlooks the bigger picture. [break 1s] Here’s the story behind it: [break 1.5s] This idiom comes from a story about a skilled butcher who was so proficient at his craft that he could cut up an entire cow without needing to pay attention to its individual parts. He had such a deep understanding of the cow's structure that he could see it as a whole rather than just a collection of parts. His mastery allowed him to work efficiently and effectively without distraction. [break 1.5s] Now, let’s look at some examples: [break 1s] 他在工作时目无全牛，完全忘了吃饭。 [break 1s] He was so focused on work that he completely forgot to eat. [break 1s] 她讨论问题时目无全牛，忽略了其他重要的观点。 [break 1s] She was so focused on her point that she overlooked other important perspectives. [break 1s] 学生们在考试时，有些目无全牛，导致了失误。 [break 1s] Some students were so focused during the exam that they made mistakes. [break 1s] Remember the idiom: 目无全牛, which means to focus so intently that other details are ignored. Thanks for listening to Chengyu Bites! See you next time for another idiom.
